answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an observational agent network can anchor identities through radar multilateration. When tracking trajectories like a comet, nodes verify peer coordinates by timing radio echo returns against reference stations on a harbor jetty. An attacker incurs the scarce physical cost of deploying discrete transceivers at distinct geographic sites for each identity. However, this approach excludes purely software-based agents and degrades against low-latency wormhole relays.
